mcat_description.short: MS Portable Toilets are prefabricated, relocatable toilet and bathroom cabin units constructed from mild steel (MS) sections and sheets, sold as complete ready-to-use structures per piece. They are used wherever permanent toilet construction is not feasible — construction sites, labour camps, events, and public sanitation projects.
mcat_description.long: MS Portable Toilets are factory-fabricated, self-contained sanitation cabin units built on a mild steel tubular/channel framework with MS or GI sheet outer cladding, waterproof interior wall panelling (Hylum/ACP/cement fibre board), and plywood or bison panel flooring. They are supplied complete with plumbing fixtures (Indian or Western commode, wash basin, taps), electrical fittings (exhaust fan, lighting), and optional water tanks, ready for immediate deployment and relocation. The product range spans single-compartment labour toilets, multi-compartment toilet blocks, combined toilet-cum-bathroom units, and urinal cabins, with sizes typically ranging from 3×3 ft to 4×6 ft footprint. Primary buyers are construction contractors, infrastructure project operators, event management companies, and government/municipal sanitation bodies procuring in bulk for site deployment.

market_context: MS Portable Toilets in India are a well-established segment of the prefabricated structures market, driven by large-scale infrastructure projects, the Swachh Bharat Mission, and construction site sanitation mandates. The dominant commercial form is a mild steel tubular-frame cabin with MS/GI sheet cladding, sold per piece to contractors and government bodies. Key product differentiators in the Indian market are commode type (Indian vs Western), cabin size (3×3 ft to 4×6 ft being most common), wall panelling material (Hylum sheet, ACP, cement fibre board), and inclusion of water tank and plumbing. The market uses 'MS' and 'mild steel' interchangeably; 'iron toilet' and 'lokhand ka toilet' are common buyer-side vernacular terms. GI (galvanised iron) variants are a close substitute and often listed alongside MS variants by the same manufacturers. No mandatory BIS IS standard specific to prefabricated MS portable toilet cabin structures was confirmed from available sources — manufacturers reference general quality compliance and international standards informally. Manufacturing hubs are concentrated in Maharashtra (Thane, Kalyan, Raigad), Gujarat (Ahmedabad), Telangana (Hyderabad), Karnataka (Bengaluru), and Andhra Pradesh (Guntur).
